newsitem.title: UK: BT sees 200 stg target price for digital box.
newsitem.headline: BT sees 200 stg target price for digital box.

text.p: A British Telecommunications executive said on Thursday that the company was interested in subsidising set-top boxes for digital television and said that sales would take off if they were priced at under 200 pounds.
"The objective is to try to achieve a price of 199 pounds," Rupert Gavin, BT Director of Internet and Multimedia Services, told reporters.

"That is the price point at which they will become a mass-market device," he added, saying that BT was interested in helping to subsidise a box with a high-specification modem capable of supplying a number of interactive services.
Gavin was speaking to reporters after giving evidence to a parliamentary select committee inquiry on the BBC and the future of broadcasting.
BT has been in talks with potential partners such as satellite broadcaster BSkyB and the BBC about subsidising the boxes which will be required to view digital television services, Gavin said.
BT acknowledges that it must convince the UK regulatory authorities that any partnership it enters to subsidise the launch of digital television would not distort competition.
It argues that regulators should allow those making the subsidies to earn a "sensible rate of return".
Gavin told the committee that digital broadcasting was already up and running in a number of countries and that Britain risked falling behind.

BSkyB plans to launch up to 200 digital satellite channels into the UK late in 1997. A terrestrial version broadcast from land-based transmitters and offering some 35 channels is expected to be available from mid-1998 and there are also plans for cable operators to move to a digital system.
